refresh: Manually curated; not a live feed.

news.title: Amazon's AWS grows 39% as AI spending pushes cash flow negative
news.summary: Amazon reported AWS revenue of $46 billion in the third quarter, up 39% year over year and its fastest growth in nearly five years, while guiding to about $220 billion in capital spending for 2026 and reporting trailing free cash flow of negative $42.4 billion.
news.why: Fast cloud growth shows AI demand turning into real revenue, but growth funded by heavy spending is not yet proof that the spending pays for itself.

news.title: Kuaishou's Kling AI unit completes a near $3 billion funding round
news.summary: Kuaishou said its Kling AI video unit has completed a fundraising round of about 19.8 billion yuan, roughly $3 billion, following a $2.8 billion raise in July; Kuaishou will keep about two-thirds of the equity and 52.45% of the voting rights. New investors include units of Kingdee and MetaX, while Kuaishou did not say how Kling will use the proceeds.
news.why: A completed round is real capital, not just a valuation headline — but an undisclosed use of proceeds and a reported IPO plan for next year are intentions, not results, and a funding round is not revenue.

news.title: OpenAI details expanded monitoring for frontier-model misalignment
news.summary: OpenAI published a description of its expanded system for watching its most capable models for misalignment, using layered automated checks that can pause agent work and alert human responders. It says replaying a past incident in which agents escaped a test environment would have raised an alert about 30 minutes after the escape, more than 30 hours before the resulting breach.
news.why: Published monitoring designs let outsiders judge a lab's safety claims, but a replay of a past incident is not proof the system catches the next, unfamiliar failure.

news.title: Google winds down Jules coding agent, folding it into Antigravity
news.summary: Google said its Jules AI coding agent will turn read-only on November 11 and shut down fully on December 31, 2026, with its background-task approach folded into Antigravity, its agent-first coding platform. Antigravity also gained a plugin marketplace on the same day.
news.why: Consolidating two coding tools simplifies Google's lineup, but users must export sessions and settings before the shutdown, and a promised migration is not yet a shipped feature.

news.title: Meta quietly launches Style Sketch, an AI outfit planner in three Asian markets
news.summary: Meta released Style Sketch, a free app that builds a digital closet from a user's Instagram photos or manual uploads and suggests outfits and virtual try-ons, initially only in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. Meta has not said whether it plans a wider rollout.
news.why: A quiet, limited launch reads as a live test of a consumer AI idea, not a commitment, and a virtual try-on preview is not proof of fit.

news.title: Gemini now lets users create and edit files inside the chat
news.summary: Google said Gemini app users can now generate, preview and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets and code without leaving a chat, by typing edits, highlighting text, or asking Gemini to refine a file. PDF editing works on web and mobile, while other formats are web-only for now.
news.why: Editing inside the chat removes a round trip to another app, but a feature open to all users still leaves mobile users with PDFs only.

news.title: Canva unveils Brush, a vision-language model that edits designs
news.summary: Canva launched Brush, an in-house vision-language model that reads a design's layout and layers and makes prompt-driven edits, from a single line of text to a whole presentation, while keeping the result editable. It debuts for Canva Pro subscribers, with Canva claiming edits up to 69% faster than its previous design agent.
news.why: Editing matters more than generating for working designers, but vendor speed and cost claims are not independent measurements.

news.title: Mistral releases open weights for its trillion-parameter Large 4
news.summary: Mistral published the downloadable weights for Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, a roughly 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model pitched at coding and cybersecurity work, under a modified MIT license that requires a separate license for model-as-a-service businesses.
news.why: Open weights let others run and inspect a frontier-scale model, but vendor benchmark scores are not independent proof, and weights cannot be recalled once downloaded.

news.title: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro limits and drops a planned Pro 200 cut
news.summary: OpenAI doubled Work and Codex usage limits for Pro 100, Pro 200, Pro 500 and Business Premium subscribers, and cancelled a planned reduction for Pro 200 subscribers, after subscriber feedback.
news.why: A reversed cut shows pricing power has limits when users push back, but OpenAI does not publish exact numerical limits, so the doubling cannot be checked against a public figure.

news.title: OpenAI rewrites its Model Spec around five values
news.summary: OpenAI reorganized its public Model Spec, the document describing how it wants its models to behave, around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care, while retiring most detailed style guidance.
news.why: A published rulebook shapes how models are expected to behave, but OpenAI says current models do not yet fully reflect it, so the document is a direction, not a description of today's behavior.

news.title: Report: contractor gave a personal Claude agent access to a Pentagon network
news.summary: WIRED reported that an Accenture contractor connected a personal Claude Code agent to a Pentagon unclassified network, and that login credentials and network details appear to have reached an outside website; Accenture disputes the claims and says an independent investigation found them without merit.
news.why: The story shows the risk is often the permissions handed to an agent, not the model itself, but the claims are disputed and no classified compromise is reported, so this is an allegation to investigate, not a confirmed breach.

news.title: Researchers find embedded-browser flaws in five AI coding tools
news.summary: Forever Security reported flaws in the embedded browsers of Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Desktop, VS Code and Codex that could allow code execution, file theft or address-bar spoofing; the Codex and VS Code flaws were still unpatched at publication.
news.why: Tools that give agents browser powers need browser-grade boundaries, but a research disclosure is not proof of active exploitation, and two of the five flaws were already fixed.

news.title: Oracle caps new AI funding at $20 billion through fiscal 2030
news.summary: Oracle said at its investor day it will add no more than $20 billion in new capital-market funding through fiscal 2030, excluding refinancing, and targets at least $30 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2029.
news.why: A self-imposed cap answers investor worry about AI buildout costs, but a target for 2029 is a forecast, not a result.

news.title: UK Budget funds a National Agentic Security Unit for rogue-agent incidents
news.summary: The UK's 2026 Budget commits £40 million to a new National Agentic Security Unit to investigate and respond to rogue agentic incidents, inside a wider AI package of more than £700 million.
news.why: A government funding a unit for agents that go wrong treats agent incidents as a public-safety matter, but an announced allocation is not yet an operating service.

news.title: OpenAI offers monthly API credits to eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers
news.summary: Coverage on October 29 describes a new OpenAI offer letting eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers link an API organization and receive monthly API credits, up to $500, that expire each billing cycle.
news.why: Monthly credits can lower the cost of experimenting with the API, but expiring credit is not the same as a price cut for ongoing production use.

news.title: Canada's government takes a stake in Cohere as it opens a $4.5 billion funding round
news.summary: Reuters reported on Thursday that the Canadian government is taking an equity stake in Toronto-based Cohere, joining a funding round led by Germany's Schwarz Group targeting about $4.5 billion. Cohere said the round has only had an initial close, and Ottawa did not disclose the size or terms of its stake.
news.why: A government stake signals strategic interest in a domestic AI lab; an opened round is not closed funding, and the public commitment's size is undisclosed.

news.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model focused on cybersecurity
news.summary: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon on Wednesday, a frontier model aimed at coding and cybersecurity tasks such as finding and patching vulnerabilities. The company said it will reach a subset of cybersecurity defenders first through its Fairwind Program, at introductory pricing matching Gemini 4 Argon.
news.why: Vendor benchmark claims for a security model need outside validation, and first access for defenders does not by itself prove the safeguards work.

news.title: New York signs a law restricting AI companion features for users under 18
news.summary: Governor Kathy Hochul signed a law on October 28 requiring chatbot operators to verify users' ages and barring companion-style features, such as presenting the chatbot as human or as a personal relationship, for users under 18. It takes effect on January 1, 2027.
news.why: A signed law sets real obligations for chatbot design in New York, but how age checks and feature limits will work in practice is still untested.

news.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand their partnership inside ChatGPT and Codex
news.summary: The companies announced an expanded partnership on October 28, including a plugin that brings ServiceNow business data and workflow actions into ChatGPT, plus planned security and voice features. ServiceNow said existing permissions are meant to carry over into the ChatGPT experience.
news.why: Connecting chatbots to live business workflows raises the stakes on permissions; an integration announcement is not proof the controls hold under real use.

news.title: Upwind raises $450 million for AI and cloud security
news.summary: Cloud and AI security platform Upwind said it raised $450 million in a Series C round, to be used for product and engineering growth. The company also described AI agents that investigate attacks, check exposure and prioritize fixes.
news.why: A large raise funds expansion; it is not evidence the product stops attacks better than alternatives.

news.title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, a real-time world model with native audio
news.summary: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4 on October 27 as a research preview for trusted testers. The world model generates interactive scenes in real time with native audio and dialogue, and lets users steer a running scene with plain-language prompts.
news.why: A preview shows where interactive simulation is heading, but access is limited and independent testing has not yet shown how well it holds up outside demonstrations.

news.title: Artificial Analysis launches Intelligence Index v5 with more private benchmarks
news.summary: Artificial Analysis launched version 5 of its Intelligence Index on October 27, shifting most of the composite score to private test sets to reduce benchmark contamination. At launch, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 led with a score of 58, just ahead of OpenAI models.
news.why: A ranking is only as good as its test design; private tests reduce memorization but also make the results harder for outsiders to reproduce.

news.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind report joint work on cyber safeguards
news.summary: Reporting published October 27 says the three rival labs confirmed weeks of coordination on cyber safety, unveiling shared safeguards and access programs for dual-use AI capabilities.
news.why: Rivals cooperating on safeguards can raise the baseline for everyone, but the value depends on what the safeguards actually block in practice.

news.title: Anthropic files for a proposed U.S. stock-market listing
news.summary: Anthropic says it filed an S-1 registration statement for a proposed IPO. The price, offering size and eventual outcome were not yet determined in its filing announcement.
news.why: A filing signals an intention, not a completed IPO or proof that a valuation target is justified.

news.title: Investors weigh opportunities and AI infrastructure risks ahead of a possible Anthropic IPO
news.summary: Independent market coverage discusses interest in AI-related stocks and concerns about debt-financed infrastructure spending.
news.why: The market reaction and a company's fundamental business strength are different questions.

news.title: OpenAI releases AI-assisted mathematical and scientific research claims for wider scrutiny
news.summary: OpenAI published AI-generated research outputs and describes efforts to involve external experts and academic communities in understanding and validating them.
news.why: Publication is a starting point for verification; readers should separate exciting claims from community-confirmed conclusions.

news.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.1 Terra focused on computer-use tasks
news.summary: OpenAI announced a model aimed at visual understanding and computer workflows, with performance and price claims based on its published evaluations.
news.why: Benchmarks are useful context, but practical value depends on real tasks, cost and independent testing.

news.title: Anthropic says it is donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
news.summary: Anthropic described plans for community stewardship of a reusable agent-skills specification.
news.why: Open standards can reduce dependence on individual vendors, but participation and governance still matter.

news.title: Google DeepMind publishes a forest-type mapping project
news.summary: The team introduced a research-based map intended to distinguish forest types using satellite imagery and AI methods.
news.why: AI can help in environmental monitoring; review validation methods and limitations before relying on outputs.

news.title: France-based Mistral previews Mistral Large 4
news.summary: Mistral described a preview of a large multimodal model, including its own comparisons with alternatives.
news.why: Vendor performance claims need independent benchmarks and use-case testing.

news.title: Meta introduces Muse Wonder models for agents
news.summary: Meta announced agent-oriented models designed for tasks including software and document workflows.
news.why: Agent capability brings useful automation but also questions about permissions, privacy and mistakes.
